clue.text: Crazy as singing lady a joke upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the words a joke are turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A pop star's gag falls flat, and someone calls it crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as singing lady' points to Lady Gaga, another pseudonym in this puzzle full of them; the word means crazy and is also the singer's stage name.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for mad or senile, a straight synonym for crazy.

clue.text: Like Voltaire, for instance, showing annoyance over one chapter

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece over another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: gall is irritation or annoyance
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Voltaire shown irritated with a chapter he has written.
explanation.walkthrough: Voltaire was the pen name of the Frenchman François-Marie Arouet, which fits the puzzle's theme of pseudonyms.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallic means French, and Voltaire was a Frenchman.

clue.text: Including name actress is changing for movie writers

indicators.note: the letters of the name abbreviation and actress is are changing their order

explanation.surface: An actress changes her name to suit the screenwriters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Including' just adds N to the letters of ACTRESS IS before 'changing' mixes them up.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenarists write film scenarios, or screenplays.

clue.text: Author using 15, finally, in case

indicators.note: one piece goes in a case, so it sits inside the box word

parts.note: a crate is a packing case

indicators.note: finally means only the last letter of the answer to clue 15 is used

parts.note: the answer to 15 down, NOM DE PLUME

explanation.surface: A writer works under a pen name, at last, in a particular case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Author' is a verb here: to author is to create. The last letter of NOM DE PLUME is E.
explanation.definitionFit: To author a work is to originate it, so the verb is a synonym of bring into being.

clue.text: Endure English fellow turning over something inherited from father

parts.note: to last is to endure

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning over means these letters are flipped to read upwards

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: An English chap puts up with what his father left him.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal of E + MAN gives NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A surname is traditionally passed down the paternal line, the family name a child takes from its father.

clue.text: This was frequently used by secret agent for cover

definitions.text: This was frequently used by secret agent for cover

parts.words: This was frequently used by secret agent for cover
parts.note: the pen name used by David Cornwell, a former MI6 officer, when writing his spy novels

explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs JOHN (6) then LE CARRE (13). The 'cover' sounds like a spy's false identity, but it is the name on the book covers of a real ex-spy turned novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: David Cornwell, once of British intelligence, published his espionage novels under this pseudonym.

clue.text: It's generally associated with appellation in ad, very oddly

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of in ad very are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: An advertisement uses a fancy designation in a peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appellation' means a name, fitting the theme, but here it is the French wine label 'appellation contrôlée', which names where the grapes were grown.
explanation.definitionFit: French wine classification ties a wine to its place of growing, so a grape estate is what such a label names.

clue.text: Name assumed by religious leader — less frequently following 6

definitions.text: Name assumed by religious leader — less frequently following 6

parts.words: Name assumed by religious leader — less frequently following 6
parts.note: a name taken by popes, rarer than John

explanation.walkthrough: Popes take a new name; John is the most used papal name, this one less so, and it follows JOHN (6) in the names of two recent popes, John Paul I and II.
explanation.definitionFit: Six popes have taken this apostle's name on election, and two more paired it with John.

clue.text: Odd aura about song, evergreen

indicators.note: odd means the letters of aura appear in a strange arrangement

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
an aria is a song in opera

explanation.surface: A strange glow surrounds a song that never fades.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the monkey puzzle tree, and also the pen name of the much-loved Guardian setter John Graham.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey puzzle genus is a conifer that keeps its leaves all year round.

clue.text: Romantic novelist, the writer embraced by a couple, contrarily

indicators.note: contrarily means the built-up letters are taken the opposite way, right to left
being embraced by a couple means sitting within the pair's letters

parts.note: a duo is a couple
the writer is the setter, who refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A romantic author is hugged by a pair who disagree.
explanation.walkthrough: I inside A DUO gives ADIUO, which 'contrarily' turns around. Ouida was the pen name of the Victorian novelist Maria Louise Ramé.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouida wrote florid Victorian romances such as Under Two Flags.

clue.text: Movie director's challenge, after initial and final cuts

indicators.note: the opening pair and closing pair of letters of challenge are cut off, leaving the inside

explanation.surface: A film-maker is challenged after edits at the start and end of a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuts' sounds like film editing. Woody Allen was born Allan Stewart Konigsberg.
explanation.definitionFit: Woody Allen is a famous American film-maker.

clue.text: Respond to warning, perhaps, for member of literary trio

parts.note: to act on something is to respond to it
a bell is one example of a warning

explanation.surface: Heed an alarm, if that is what it is, to join a famous trio of writers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brontë sisters published as Currer, Ellis and Acton Bell; Acton was Anne.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Brontë wrote under this male pen name, one of three sisters who did the same.

clue.text: See 6
In so-called City of Angels owns capital

indicators.note: one piece goes in another, so the letters for owns sit within the city abbreviation

parts.note: Los Angeles is nicknamed the City of Angels, abbreviated LA
has means owns

explanation.surface: Los Angeles possesses a lot of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is the city: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the chief city of Tibet, the seat of its government.

clue.text: American author from a city in US returned foreign currency

indicators.note: returned means these letters are read back the other way

parts.note: NY is New York, a US city
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Someone back from an American city brings foreign money.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayn Rand was the pen name of the Russian-born novelist Alisa Rosenbaum.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayn Rand wrote The Fountainhead and Atlas Shrugged in the United States.

clue.text: Molière, for example, in his own language

definitions.text: Molière, for example, in his own language

parts.words: Molière, for example, in his own language
parts.note: Molière was the stage name of Jean-Baptiste Poquelin, and the French phrase for a writer's pen name is wanted

explanation.walkthrough: 'in his own language' asks for the French term rather than the English 'pen name'.
explanation.definitionFit: Molière is a pseudonym, and the expression used in English for a pseudonym is borrowed from French.

clue.text: First name of composer of verses used by another for 5

definitions.text: First name of composer of verses used by another for 5

parts.words: First name of composer of verses used by another for 5
parts.note: the poet Thomas had this forename, which the singer born Robert Zimmerman took as his surname

explanation.walkthrough: 5 is LAST NAME. The Welsh poet Dylan Thomas's first name became the last name of Bob Dylan.
explanation.definitionFit: Bob Dylan, born Zimmerman, took his stage surname from the forename of Dylan Thomas.

clue.text: A voyage back as result of making a name for oneself

definitions.text: result of making a name for oneself

indicators.note: back means the letters for the voyage are read backwards

parts.note: a sail is a trip by boat, a voyage

explanation.surface: A sea trip home makes someone famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making a name for oneself' usually means becoming famous; here it means literally inventing a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: An alias is a false name someone adopts, so inventing a name for yourself gives you one.

clue.text: Two names I later falsified, under cover?

indicators.note: falsified means these letters are doctored into a different arrangement

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name, so two names give NN

explanation.surface: Someone forges two false names later, to stay under cover as a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under cover' suggests a spy, but the question mark points to the literal sense: under a cover, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something internal lies inside, as if covered by an outer layer.

clue.text: MI6 man sounded signal

indicators.note: sounded means the letter is said aloud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: Q is the quartermaster of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A British spy gave a signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cue is a prompt or signal for someone to act, as an actor's line.

clue.text: Eg Astaire and Rogers often consuming last of tinned fruit

indicators.note: consuming means one piece swallows another, so the end letter sits inside

parts.note: Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers often starred together, so they were co-stars

indicators.note: last of means only the final letter of tinned is used

explanation.surface: A dancing pair eat tinned fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Costards are a large old English variety of cooking apple.

clue.text: 15 muddles men up with this poser

indicators.note: the letters of NOM DE PLUME are jumbled together with men up's letters, which is what muddles signals

parts.note: the answer to 15 down, NOM DE PLUME

explanation.surface: A pen name gets mixed up with some men and a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus MEN UP, rearranged, gives NOM DE PLUME. 'poser' reads like a puzzle but means one who poses.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or photographer's model is someone who sits or stands for them in a pose.

clue.text: Lacking leaders in war, it lists talented people like David and 6

indicators.note: each of the words war, it and lists is lacking its leading letter

explanation.surface: A list of talented wartime people with nobody to lead them.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is JOHN: the painters Jacques-Louis David and Augustus John.
explanation.definitionFit: David and Augustus John are both famous painters, examples of creative people.

clue.text: I tear into outlaw

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to ban is to outlaw
to rend is to tear

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I' is the setter speaking: Brendan is this puzzle's pseudonymous setter, and 'outlaw' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter of this crossword signs as Brendan, so the first person in a clue means the setter.

clue.text: Relies on unknown artist who wants to remain unknown

definitions.text: artist who wants to remain unknown

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: banks, as in banks on, means relies
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone relies on an artist who wants to stay anonymous.
explanation.walkthrough: Banksy is the British street artist whose real identity has never been officially confirmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksy is a graffiti artist known for keeping their identity secret.

clue.text: Name of poet thus shown in this kind of clue

indicators.note: shown in means the word for thus appears inside the other word

parts.note: this is a down clue, so the word is DOWN
so means thus

explanation.surface: A poet's name is demonstrated by this type of clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Ernest Dowson was an English poet of the 1890s.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest Dowson wrote the line 'days of wine and roses' and was a decadent poet.

clue.text: American author or two added to religious book

indicators.note: one piece added to another follows it

parts.note: Mark is a gospel, a book of the Bible
twain is an old word for two

explanation.surface: An American writer, or a pair of them, adds to a holy book.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark Twain was the pen name of Samuel Clemens.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn and is a famous American writer.

clue.text: Huge upset for one of the Stones?

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means these letters are turned upside down, reading upwards

parts.note: a gem is a precious stone, so one is a gem; the question mark flags that the Rolling Stones are not meant

explanation.surface: A Rolling Stones member is very upset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stones' with a capital suggests the band, but it means gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Mega is a slang word for very great or enormous.

clue.text: It's up to old European statesman

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters of it read upwards

explanation.surface: It is the responsibility of an elder European politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's up to' reads as a stock phrase about responsibility, but 'up' is the reversal signal in this down clue. Tito was the alias of the Yugoslav leader Josip Broz.
explanation.definitionFit: Josip Broz, known as Tito, led Yugoslavia from 1945 to 1980.

clue.text: Real name, last but not first, of Oxford don

definitions.text: Real name, last but not first, of Oxford don

parts.words: Real name, last but not first, of Oxford don
parts.note: the real surname, not the forename Clive, of the Oxford don who wrote the Narnia books

explanation.walkthrough: Unlike the pen names around it, this is a genuine surname, the last name but not the first of C. S. Lewis, the Oxford academic. It is also the forename of Lewis Carroll, an Oxford don's pen name.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive Staples Lewis taught English at Oxford and wrote the Narnia books under his own surname.

clue.text: Eg Brendan finishes off tricky puzzle that's irritating to face

parts.note: Saint Brendan is an example of a saint, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: finishes off means the end letters of tricky and puzzle are taken

explanation.surface: The setter completes a hard crossword that gets on everyone's nerves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brendan' looks like the setter but it is St Brendan, the Irish saint known as the Navigator.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, a sore spot on the face.

clue.text: Present and original name for Hugh, but not Cary

definitions.meaning: to present something is to ... it, or a ... is a gift

definitions.text: original name for Hugh, but not Cary
definitions.meaning: Hugh ... was born with this surname, while Cary ... was born Archibald Leach

explanation.surface: A gift and a birth name shared by one film star but not the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is something given, a synonym of a gift; and Hugh Grant was born a Grant, while Cary Grant took the name.

clue.text: Free from material constraints, doctor sided with boy hiding spy

indicators.note: hiding means the shuffled letters contain the spy's letter hidden within them
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of sided and boy are rearranged

parts.note: M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories, a spymaster

explanation.surface: A doctor teams up with a boy who is sheltering a spy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' is a verb, rearranging SIDED and BOY into DISEBODY, which then takes M inside. 'doctor' looks like the abbreviation DR, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To disembody is to separate a spirit from its body, freeing it from physical form.
